text: TLH telemetry should use an anonymous persistent UUID so launch analytics can report per-user sessions. This supersedes an identifierless-only design: the goal is still not to collect personal information, cwd, arguments, settings, or other metadata, but a stable per-install anonymous clientUser is acceptable for counting users/sessions.

TLH telemetry should include a small metadata payload for model, OS, and TLH version in addition to an anonymous persistent per-install clientUser. It still should not include cwd, prompts, args, hostname, username, repo names, settings, or other potentially identifying local context.

TLH telemetry OS metadata should be more specific than a coarse platform string. Send human-readable OS family and version information, while still avoiding hostname, username, hardware serials, cwd, repo names, prompts, args, and other local context.

TLH telemetry opt-outs must persist across updates. If a user sets the isolated settings opt-out (tlh.telemetry.enabled=false), installer reruns and tlh update must preserve that value and must not re-enable telemetry unless the user explicitly opts back in.

For TLH launch telemetry, the TelemetryDeck namespace/appID are intentionally embedded as public client analytics identifiers; they are not treated as secrets. The current model payload policy keeps a privacy-filtered/public-looking model value rather than switching to coarse provider-only buckets; the user accepted this tradeoff after oracle review.

Before making a TLH release, verify local main is up to date with origin/main and has no divergence. A release tag pushed from a local-only commit can publish successfully while main push is rejected, leaving the GitHub Release tag ahead of origin/main until the branches are reconciled.
Human wants to start breaking down install.sh because the installer has grown too large; favor an incremental, behavior-preserving decomposition rather than broad rewrites.
